from_ecto_schema is documented as 'not necessarily optimal, nor support all Ecto types' — it is a pragmatic generator, not a complete JSON Schema compiler. geex commands with unusual arg types may need custom mapping beyond what instructor_ex covers.

instructor_ex is an Elixir library tightly coupled to Ecto. If geex is not an Elixir/Ecto codebase, you cannot 'adopt' it — only reimplement the technique. The report assumes geex MAY be Elixir; confirm geex's host language before choosing adopt vs adapt for Direction A.

The reask/max_retries loop assumes geex controls the LLM call. In the MCP-server (LLM-calls-geex) direction the calling host owns the retry loop, so instructor_ex's headline retry feature does NOT transfer to Direction B — geex should instead return MCP isError + formatted validation messages and let the host self-correct.

Adopting instructor_ex for Direction B would create a SECOND source of truth (an Ecto schema per command) competing with the macro DSL, violating geex's commands-as-data single-authority model. This is the central architectural conflict to avoid.

distilled.headline: Yes — geex-commands, Jido-actions, balance_beam-schemas, and instructor_ex-Ecto-schemas are four projections of ONE abstraction: a typed, schema-bearing, runnable operation (a value carrying its arg-types, a JSON-Schema derivable from those types, a validator, and a runner). geex should define this once as the macro-generated Command and derive everything downstream from it: minibuffer parse, MCP inputSchema, inbound-LLM-arg coercion/validation, prompt synthesis, undo entry, and collab op. The single hard non-negotiable that distinguishes geex from all four libraries is that the command must be a VALUE (a %Command.X{} struct), not a module+map (Jido) or an Ecto schema owning its own definition (instructor_ex/balance_beam) — because undo, replay, macro-recording, serialization and collab determinism all require the operation to be a serializable value. The transport story collapses to: in-VM BEAM message passing is the default for everything co-located (geex<->pharos, geex<->first-party agent), and MCP/JSON-RPC is strictly a thin external adapter for foreign/untrusted clients, never an internal write path. The AI loop is bidirectional and the two directions want different libraries: instructor_ex's technique (not the library) backs geex-calls-LLM, and geex's own dispatcher (not Jido) backs LLM-calls-geex.
distilled.transport_recommendation:
Treat transport as a function of the boundary being crossed (process, language, trust), not a single global choice. Decision table for geex:

(1) geex <-> pharos (LSP), co-located on one BEAM node: IN-VM BEAM MESSAGING / direct process calls. pharos is Gleam-on-BEAM, geex is Elixir-on-BEAM; share warm LSP pool processes via Erlang terms (GenServer.call / send), no JSON, no WebSocket, no TLS, no plugin/conformance stack. This is the single biggest free win — the entire pharos "universal editor bridge" (ADR-028, WebSocket + handshake + per-editor plugin repos + conformance harness) exists only to cross an out-of-VM boundary geex does not have. Take the bridge's SEMANTIC contract (Tier-1 didOpen/didChange live-doc mirroring; editor_focus = {active_uri, cursor, selection, viewport, open_files}; reverse-channel showDiff/diagnostics/progress) and realize it as an in-VM API, NOT a socket. Caveat: pharos currently exposes only stdio/HTTP MCP transports; geex likely must get pharos to add an in-VM entry point to its LSP pool, or fall back to (2). Also inherit the bridge's Tier-1 problem: didChange shadow state (unsaved buffers) must not leak into queries expecting on-disk truth.

(2) geex spawning pharos as a child when NOT co-located, or talking to any external MCP server: STDIO JSON-RPC. Subprocess over a Port. This is the portable fallback and what v0.5 ships for pharos if the in-VM API isn't ready. Mirror pharos's daemon design only if geex ever exposes its own out-of-VM services: idle-timeout-instead-of-EOF lifecycle + well-known socket auto-discover-or-spawn-ephemeral.

(3) geex first-party in-pane AI agent: IN-VM, NO transport at all — the agent is a BEAM process in geex's supervision tree that calls Dispatch.run/1 directly. JSON-RPC to your own VM buys nothing but serialization overhead.

(4) Foreign/untrusted MCP clients (claude-code, Cursor, BYO-agent): STDIO JSON-RPC (or unix socket / HTTP). The process boundary IS the sandbox — a subprocess speaking JSON can only emit command structs, never run code in your VM. This is the ONLY safe door for untrusted agents.

(5) geex <-> geex across machines (remote dev, collab, LSP-on-bigger-box): DISTRIBUTED ERLANG via :erpc.call/5 (not legacy :rpc — better per-call timeouts and exception propagation), but ONLY for infrastructure you own. Distributed Erlang's trust model is binary: a node that passes cookie auth can run arbitrary code via :erpc (halt your VM, read all ETS, message any process), and connections auto-mesh transitively. NEVER model untrusted collab peers or third-party agents as dist nodes. Use -hidden + inet_tls_dist + strong cookies for owned nodes; route everyone else through the dispatcher allowlist (or wasmex). Correct the notes' collab tagline: {BufferPid, Node@host} ! msg is invalid syntax — use a bare remote pid (pid ! msg) or send({:registered_name, :"geex@host"}, msg); resolve remote handles via :pg (partition-tolerant), never :global (its netsplit-heal can kill a process), and re-resolve on every :nodedown since remote pids die permanently across a node restart.

WHAT v0.5 SHIPS: in-VM dispatcher as the single internal interface; in-VM (or stdio-fallback) pharos integration; one stdio MCP server adapter for external/untrusted clients; first-party agent as an in-VM process. Defer distributed-Erlang collab and any HTTP/TLS/daemon to post-v0.5 — they're owned-infra and remote-collab concerns, not v0.5 critical path. The collab transport is trivial; the CONSISTENCY layer (CRDT) is the real work and is independent of transport.
distilled.ai_loop_recommendation:
The AI loop is bidirectional and the two directions are asymmetric — pick the backing library per direction, and in both cases reuse a TECHNIQUE rather than importing a framework, because geex's command DSL must remain the single source of truth.

DIRECTION A — geex CALLS the LLM (in-editor AI command: "turn this prose into a geex macro", "suggest a command", "rename across codebase"): back this with instructor_ex's pattern, and since geex IS an Elixir app you can depend on instructor_ex directly for the model-call plumbing — define an Ecto embedded_schema for the AI's EXPECTED OUTPUT (note: this is the model's response contract, NOT a competing definition of a geex command, so no source-of-truth conflict), call Instructor.chat_completion(model:, response_model:, max_retries:, messages:) and get {:ok, struct} | {:error, changeset}. The single most valuable, portable idea to steal wholesale is the reask loop: on validation failure, format the changeset errors as text, append them + the model's prior tool-call echo + a "fix these errors" message, decrement a retry budget, recurse. instructor_ex's Adapter behaviour already covers Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/Ollama/local, so geex gets model-agnosticism for the calling side for free. geex drives the loop here, so retries belong to geex.

DIRECTION B — the LLM CALLS geex (MCP tool export; inbound JSON args must become a Command struct): back this with geex's OWN dispatcher; do NOT adopt Jido or instructor_ex as the library here. The MCP server is a ~20-line adapter: JSON params -> CommandRegistry.lookup(name).parse(params) -> Dispatch.run(struct) — identical tail to the minibuffer path and the in-VM-agent path. Reuse THREE techniques from instructor_ex against the command AST (not Ecto): (i) the Ecto-type -> JSON-Schema mapping table + $defs/$ref BFS for nested args; (ii) a cast/coerce step turning loose JSON ("3"->3, string->enum atom) into typed Command fields; (iii) error-string formatting — but here geex does NOT own retries (the calling host does), so on bad args return MCP isError:true with formatted validation messages and let the host self-correct. Deliberately DIVERGE from instructor_ex on one thing: it marks every field `required` and pushes optionality into validation; geex must emit accurate required/optional arrays from the DSL arg specs so the calling model gets correct hints. Also prefer CLOSED/strict validation (reject unknown args) over Jido's open/chaining semantics — an editor wants a typo'd LLM command rejected, not silently accepted.

THE SECURITY PAYOFF HIDING IN THIS DESIGN: because the dispatcher only ever executes known, schema-validated command structs (an allowlist, never arbitrary code), it is simultaneously the universal call interface AND the security chokepoint. Route every untrusted party — MCP client, remote human collaborator, sandboxed agent — through it. For untrusted IN-VM extension/agent code that needs more than command-dispatch, use wasmex (the only strong in-process BEAM sandbox) with its host export surface bottoming out at Dispatch.run/1. PIDs-as-capabilities (the notes' gem) is real in-VM hygiene but gates only messaging (not File/:os.cmd/Code.eval) and is not a network boundary — treat as discipline, not sandbox.
distilled.convergence_insight:
YES — and this is the load-bearing finding. All four describe the SAME object: a typed, schema-bearing, runnable operation = (a) a set of typed named arguments, (b) a JSON Schema mechanically derivable from those types, (c) a validator/coercer that turns loose input into the typed form, (d) a runner that executes it against some state. geex-command, Jido.Action, balance_beam-schema, and instructor_ex-Ecto-schema are four PROJECTIONS of this one abstraction, each library having independently re-derived "one declaration -> {struct/validator, JSON schema, prompt fragments, runner/tool}" (instructor_ex's from_ecto_schema, Jido's to_tool/0 + Jido.Exec, balance_beam's explicit "Schema -> struct+validator / JSON schema / prompt fragments / effect wrappers" diagram, geex's macro generating struct+parser+runner+JSON-schema). The convergence is genuine, not coincidental.

THE UNIFIED ABSTRACTION geex should define ONCE: a macro-generated Command where the command IS A VALUE (%Command.Copy{range:, name:}), carrying enough compile-time metadata to derive every downstream artifact. From the single `command :copy do arg ... run ... end` block, geex generates: (1) the struct + a typed constructor; (2) the minibuffer parser (arg-type-aware: :coord_range parses "a1-g3"); (3) the runner run(%Command.Copy{}, state); (4) the MCP inputSchema (JSON Schema via the instructor_ex-style type-mapping + $defs technique, with ACCURATE required arrays); (5) the inbound-JSON coercer/validator for the LLM-calls-geex path (instructor_ex's cast technique, closed/strict); (6) help text; (7) optionally a prompt fragment for the geex-calls-LLM path; (8) the undo-history entry (the executed struct itself); (9) the collab op (serialize the struct). Items 4-8 all fall out of items 1-3 for free — that is the "all consumers for the price of one DSL block" property the notes already bet on, now confirmed to be exactly what three external libraries each rebuilt.

WHERE geex MUST DIVERGE from each, and why: (a) Jido passes a validated MAP to run(params, ctx) and reserves structs for agent state — it does NOT defstruct the arguments. geex CANNOT accept this: command-as-value is the whole point (undo/replay/macro-recording/serialization/collab-determinism). Adopt jido_action's macro/schema/to_tool DESIGN as a blueprint and possibly depend on jido_action narrowly, but keep geex's own thin command-as-value struct + synchronous editor-state dispatcher on top; SKIP Jido's agent/signal/sensor/directive runtime entirely (it is autonomous-agent machinery, wrong-shaped for synchronous local editor ops where determinism beats autonomy). (b) instructor_ex / balance_beam make an Ecto schema the authority and DERIVE the command from it — geex must invert this: the macro-DSL command is the authority and the JSON-Schema/validator are derived FROM it. Do NOT introduce a per-command Ecto schema; that splits the source of truth and breaks commands-as-data. (c) From balance_beam, do NOT take the "Ecto for LLMs" thesis (the author retracted it) — take its REVISED stance and two primitives: the @bb_effects compile-time-wrapper pattern (a per-command effect list like [:validate, :provenance, :budget] that mechanically installs wrappers, making the human-vs-LLM dispatch difference DECLARATIVE rather than branch logic — a human-dispatched command skips :llm but keeps :provenance, an LLM-dispatched one adds :validate/:tool_call), and the provenance/trust model: when a command is LLM-originated, attach a __provenance__ field (model, prompt version, cost, retries) to the very same struct that lives in undo history, so "provenance entry" and "undo entry" become the SAME object — audit-grade undo for free. Also adopt balance_beam's "no failure path loses provenance" invariant and its Untrusted.t()/delimit_isolate trust-wrapping for LLM-sourced string args (runtime enforcement in Elixir; the compile-time-strong version needs the Gleam typed boundary geex already plans for its extension API).

NET PRESCRIPTION: define Geex.Command (macro DSL -> value-struct + parser + runner + derived JSON schema + derived coercer) as the ONE abstraction. Layer instructor_ex's schema-derivation and reask TECHNIQUES, balance_beam's effect-annotation + provenance/trust DESIGN, and optionally jido_action's macro as a reference/narrow-dependency — but the command-as-value struct and the synchronous dispatcher are geex's own and are not delegated to any of them.

The reask loop (format changeset errors -> append + prior-turn echo -> recurse) is the single most valuable portable idea. For the LLM-CALLS-geex direction, do NOT depend on it (would create a second Ecto source-of-truth competing with the command DSL) — instead reimplement three techniques against the command AST: type->JSON-Schema mapping + $defs/$ref BFS, the cast/coerce step, error-string formatting. (b) Hand-roll Geex.Command from scratch — full control, command-as-value native, no upstream churn, but reimplement JSON-Schema generation (weeks per the research) and an MCP server.
open_decisions.recommendation: Hand-roll Geex.Command (the value-struct + parser + runner + dispatcher), because command-as-value and a synchronous deterministic editor dispatcher are the project's core bet and Jido fights both. BUT lift jido_action's macro shape and to_tool/0 design as a blueprint, and lift instructor_ex's from_ecto_schema type-mapping + $defs technique for the JSON-Schema generator so you don't reinvent that hard part. Re-evaluate a narrow jido_action dependency only if hand-rolling the schema generator proves more than ~1 week.

open_decisions.question: One Command abstraction for both human and LLM, or split paths?
open_decisions.options: (a) ONE abstraction, dispatch difference expressed declaratively via a per-command effect list (balance_beam @bb_effects style: human skips :llm/:validate but keeps :provenance; LLM adds :validate/:tool_call/provenance-wrapping). (b) Separate LLM command surface.
open_decisions.recommendation: ONE abstraction — it is the entire architectural through-line ('one vocabulary, one dispatcher, one history'). Make the human-vs-LLM difference a declarative effect annotation that installs wrappers (validation/provenance/trust) around the same Dispatch.run/1, not a parallel code path. This is the convergence cashed out concretely.

open_decisions.question: Does the same Command struct serve as both undo entry and AI-provenance record?
open_decisions.options: (a) Same struct gains an optional __provenance__ field populated only on LLM origin (model, prompt version, cost, retries, cassette segment); undo entry == provenance entry. (b) Separate audit log alongside undo history.
open_decisions.recommendation: Same struct with optional __provenance__ — since executed commands are already the recorded undo entries, attaching provenance makes AI undo entries audit-grade for free and keeps one history. Adopt balance_beam's 'no failure path loses provenance' invariant so even rejected/failed LLM commands leave an auditable trace.

open_decisions.question: Closed (strict) vs open (chaining) argument validation for commands?
open_decisions.options: (a) Closed/strict — reject unknown/typo'd args (instructor_ex-ish, but with accurate required arrays). (b) Open — extras pass through (Jido's chaining semantics).
open_decisions.recommendation: Closed/strict. An editor must reject a malformed LLM or plugin command, not silently accept it; chaining is an agent-pipeline concern geex doesn't need at the command layer. Emit accurate required/optional in the MCP inputSchema (do NOT copy instructor_ex's all-fields-required behavior).

open_decisions.question: How does geex integrate pharos's LSP — in-VM or stdio — for v0.5?
open_decisions.options: (a) In-VM BEAM messaging to pharos's shared LSP pool (fastest, no serialization) but pharos exposes no documented in-VM API today and you'd inherit the unsaved-buffer-vs-disk consistency problem. (b) stdio JSON-RPC MCP subprocess (works today, portable, but serialization + process boundary).
open_decisions.recommendation: Target in-VM as the architectural end-state (it's the free win that justifies geex being on the same BEAM as pharos) but SHIP stdio for v0.5 as the pragmatic path, since the in-VM pool entry point is not a documented pharos surface yet. Open a concrete ask to pharos: expose an in-VM API to the workspace-keyed LSP pool. Keep the MCP-server-as-thin-adapter shape so swapping stdio->in-VM later touches only the transport leaf, mirroring the notes' interchangeable-frontend principle.

open_decisions.question: When does collab/distributed-Erlang and HTTP/TLS/daemon enter the roadmap?
open_decisions.options: (a) Design transport hooks now, defer implementation. (b) Build collab transport early.
open_decisions.recommendation: Defer both past v0.5. The dispatcher-as-single-interface design already makes :erpc and CRDT-backed collab a later additive layer ('AI/remote node is just another participant'), and the real collab cost is the CRDT consistency model, not transport. v0.5 ships in-VM dispatcher + (stdio or in-VM) pharos + one stdio MCP adapter + first-party in-VM agent. HTTP/TLS/daemon are owned-infra/remote concerns with no v0.5 justification.
